title.narrative: Increased labour compliance and implementation of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH)

description.narrative: Indonesia faces unique challenges for labour law compliance because of its large workforce that is spread across 38 provinces and thousands of islands. Despite positive recent institutional and human resource developments, the capacity of the inspectorate remains modest relative to the size of the workforce and the rapid growth and modernization, as well as diversification of economic activities. In addition, the decentralization of the inspection system across the country which has diminished the capacity of the central inspection authority in implementing inspection policies and practices uniformly across the provinces. To address these issues, a strategic approach to assure compliance with labour regulations is necessary. It could draw on complementary interventions towards strengthening workplace compliance such as enforcement, awareness raising, social partnership and effective industrial relations. The compliance with labour regulations and occupational safety and health (OSH) are important enablers of sustainable business and workers’ welfare. Tripartite constituents agreed to advance these two aspects by improving labour inspection system and preventing work accidents and occupational disease. In addition to the Government’s responsibilities, a collaborative framework involving social partners at both national, regional and sectoral levels, as well as the effective operationalization of the OSH Committee at the enterprise level (P2K3). Efforts are also directed to strengthen promotional and outreach capabilities through enterprise level initiatives. This work is particularly relevant in the light of the ILO technical assistance and capacity development in certain sectors such as garment, palm oil and fishing and specific target for people living with HIV/Aids, persons with disability, young workers, and women in rural sector.
